messages:
maya: heads up — sketching a lightweight handoff protocol for moving pages off the GPU without introducing global stalls. goal: minimize tail latency when we need to evict model tensors mid-request.

zack: sounds useful. current problem summary?

maya: when a big request needs memory we either synchronously stall or trigger async copy+block. both cause tail spikes or require lots of pinned staging. idea: cooperative handoff where the GPU owner yields pages to a host-side 'carrying' worker with a handshake, so the compute can continue using a placeholder until the page is fully migrated.

anika: by placeholder you mean a thin proxy that returns zero/placeholder tokens until the real page comes back? that seems risky for correctness.

maya: sorry wording — placeholder = a small metadata token kept in the request path that marks data as 'in-flight'. compute continues on non-dependent paths; dependent ops will wait only on the specific token rather than whole-context stall.

zack: ok. propose message flow:
```
HANDOFF_INIT(pid, page_id, size) -> host
HANDOFF_ACK(accept_token) -> gpu-owner
START_COPY(page_id, dma_handle)  // gpu->host async
COPY_DONE(page_id, crc) -> host
RELINQUISH(page_id) -> gpu-owner (owner removes residency)
```
An owner can revoke if copy fails.

anika: who runs the host-side carrying worker? per-node daemon or per-process thread? concurrency model matters for PCIe link saturation.

maya: node-level worker pool with per-GPU lanes. we track active handoffs per-lane to avoid saturating PCIe. lanes are soft quotas tuned by telemetry.

zack: need backpressure signals in case host is overloaded. maybe HANDOFF_NACK(reason) with suggested wait-window. also we need to prefer prefetch vs. urgent handoff.

maya: agreed. add HANDOFF_NACK(retry_after_ms) and HINT_PREFETCH(timestamp, priority) for predictive prefetching.

runtime-bot: telemetry: recent trace shows average handoff copy 7.2ms, 99p 35ms over PCIe gen3 on our test cluster: https://telemetry.redwood/internal/hand-off/pci

anika: two correctness concerns: 1) concurrent writers -> we must maintain write-serialization (ownership tokens) 2) GPU-side references must not be freed until RELINQUISH ack.

maya: ownership token model: owner grants a single mutable token and any number of read tokens. handoff requires owner to convert mutable token to a transient read token and issue HANDOFF_INIT; upon RELINQUISH the owner drops token. Full semantics in this snippet:
```
// owner: has MUTABLE_T
owner: convert MUTABLE_T -> TRANSIENT_READ_T
owner: HANDOFF_INIT(page)
// host: copies page, returns ACCEPT_T
owner: on RELINQUISH remove MUTABLE_T from table
```

zack: sounds ok. we should define timeouts and auto-rollbacks: if COPY_DONE not observed in X ms, host returns FAIL and owner reacquires MUTABLE_T and resumes. also record failure metric.

anika: what about fragmented allocations? migrating a 4MB page vs 64KB subpages has different cost. support variable granularity in HANDOFF_INIT?

maya: yes, HANDOFF_INIT can include subrange descriptors. default granularity is 256KB; smaller allowed but marked high cost and lower prefetch priority.

zack: ops for compacting: host can coalesce adjacent carried subpages into a single slab during idle periods. add HOST_COMPACT(page_range) telemetry event.

maya: actionable items: 1) sketch protocol RFC (maya) 2) simulation microbench for copy latency and lane-saturation (zack) 3) ownership token API changes and timeouts (anika) 4) add telemetry events for HANDOFF_* and HOST_COMPACT (runtime-bot for infra).

anika: +1 on RFC. let's call out fail cases explicitly: pci-reset, copy CRC mismatch, host OOM.

zack: I'll prototype a fake lane scheduler to test backpressure heuristics.

maya: ok I'll draft the RFC tonight and post link. feel free to ping me with edge cases. :thumbsup:
